headline: Quiet Day In The Hub Means Reliving Ultimate Red Sox Glory
morning_brew: Quiet day in the Hub, which reminds me of a night back in October 2004 during the ALCS. We were down three games to zero against the Yankees, and I was sitting at a bar in Southie watching Game 4. Uncle Carmine had actually fallen asleep on his barstool by the sixth inning, and when he woke up in the seventh, he grumbled and headed home to Revere because he thought the season was completely over. I almost followed him out the door, feeling that old familiar knot in my stomach, while the bartender started wiping down the counter and some guy in a Pedro Martinez jersey was literally crying into his plate of nachos.

Then came the bottom of the ninth, we got a guy on first base, and Dave Roberts came in to pinch run. Everyone in the building knew he was going, and he still slid into second just ahead of the tag. The entire bar absolutely lost its mind, beer was flying, and Uncle Carmine apparently heard the scream all the way on the Southeast Expressway. We went on to break that eighty-six-year Curse of the Bambino, but it all started with that one slide.

Looking ahead to tomorrow, the Red Sox are finally back at Fenway Park to open up a series against the Texas Rangers. Ranger Suarez is slated to get the ball, and we desperately need a win to snap this brutal four-game losing streak. The Patriots are still wrapping up minicamp down in Foxborough, where Drake Maye is busy building chemistry with A.J. Brown, so at least there is some hope on the horizon.

news_digest.headline: Drake Maye embracing Patriots team culture
news_digest.dans_take: Love seeing the young quarterback step up and lead by example down in Foxborough.
